<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #42616

Problem Summary:

Currently there is no way to partition a non partitioned table or remove partitioning from a partitioned table.
Also there is currently no support for alter a table to a different partitioning scheme.

### What is changed and how it works?

Building upon Reorganize Partition, which does all the data copying and recreating the indexes, we can now support ALTER TABLE t REMOVE PARTITIONING and ALTER TABLE t PARTITION BY ...

### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [ ] Unit test
- [x] Integration test
- [ ] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
- [ ] No code

Side effects

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU
- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory
- [ ] Breaking backward compatibility

Documentation

- [ ] Affects user behaviors
- [ ] Contains syntax changes
- [ ] Contains variable changes
- [ ] Contains experimental features
- [x] Changes MySQL compatibility

### Release note

<!-- compatibility change, improvement, bugfix, and new feature need a release note -->

Please refer to [Release Notes Language Style Guide](https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/release-notes-style-guide.html) to write a quality release note.

```release-note
Added support for ALTER TABLE t PARTITION BY and ALTER TABLE t REMOVE PARTITIONING
```

issue_context.title: Support ALTER TABLE t REMOVE PARTITIONING
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

There are no ways to alter a table between partitioned and non-partitioned (unless you renaming tables and using exchange partition to move the data into a partitioned table).

This enhancement is to support `ALTER TABLE t REMOVE PARTITIONING`.
Also making clear if such operation would allow other DDL operations in the same statement (like changing columns etc.)

Another related enhancement would be to support `ALTER TABLE t PARTITION BY ...` to (re)partition a table with a new partitioning scheme.

Tasks:
- [x] Implement `ALTER TABLE t REMOVE PARTITIONING` https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/42907
- [x] Implement `ALTER TABLE t PARTITION BY ...` https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/42907
- [x] Document the new features https://github.com/pingcap/docs/pull/13167
- [x] Implement support for the above in TiCDC https://github.com/pingcap/tiflow/pull/9670
- [x] Implement support for the above in TiFlash https://github.com/pingcap/tiflash/pull/7822
- [x] Add tests for placement rule https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/47337
- [x] Add tests for auto id https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/46909 (Note also affected by https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/46904)
- [ ] Add tests for nonclustered tables
- [ ] Add tests for statistics
- [ ] Add tests for combining with other features
  - [ ] CHECK Constraint
  - [ ] ...
- [ ] Add tests for tools like BR etc.
- [x] Declare the features GA and update the documentation

Note: FOREIGN Key is not yet supported with Partitioned Tables, so no need to test it, see https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/46960.

review_comments: Will this lock the handle for a long time and make accessing statistics data block?

It is modelled after `insertTableStats2KV`. The function will execute 7 internal update statements (change the table ids in each of the stats_* tables, within one transaction, so I expect it to be quick, and during the time it will block accessing non-cached statistics data, and variables.
